hook: If you lie in bed for 45 minutes unable to turn your brain off, your body hasn't been given the right signal to sleep — and it's probably been happening for hours before you got into bed.
topic: Sleep onset latency — why the 60-minute pre-sleep window is the real determinant
body:
**If it takes you 30, 40, 45 minutes to fall asleep most nights — the problem didn't start when you got into bed. It started about an hour before that.**

Sleep onset requires a specific biological sequence. Your core body temperature needs to drop. Cortisol needs to be low and falling. The brain needs a reduction in novel stimulation that would signal wakefulness.

When you're scrolling, watching something with narrative tension, having a difficult conversation, or running through tomorrow's task list while lying in the dark — you're feeding the exact inputs that keep the wakefulness system active.

The brain doesn't switch off like a light. It transitions through a gradient that you either support or disrupt in the window before bed.

The 60 minutes before sleep is not downtime. It is the most important variable in your sleep onset time. What you do in that window determines whether you're asleep in 12 minutes or staring at the ceiling for an hour.

One specific protocol for that window — it's linked in my bio.
